mechanics.body_shape: read the array's begin and end, count its elements with a magic-multiply division by the 0xac stride, scan indices 0..count-1 for the element whose +0xa8 word equals the argument, and on a match shift every later element down one 0xac slot (skipping the shift when the match is the last element) and drop the end word by 0xac. AL is 0 when nothing matched and 1 when something did.

frame_resolution.method: one linear walk of ESP through all 46 instructions. Entry ESP is 0 in the walk; the prologue pushes three words (entry-4 EBX, entry-8 ESI, entry-12 EDI), the single call is cdecl and cleaned by the body at 0x00fa55ef, and each epilogue pops the same three in reverse, so the walk ends on entry ESP and `RET 0x4` consumes the return address plus the one argument word.
frame_resolution.corroboration: two independent agreements. (1) 0x00fa55ae reads [ESP+0x10] with the ESP in effect at entry-12, which is entry+4, the single argument slot -- and entry+4 is the only slot a balanced frame leaves free. (2) both return sites are the same three bytes, `C2 04 00`, so the two paths agree on the cleanup, and the model test MEASURES it rather than asserting it: a trampoline pushes the argument word, samples ESP, calls, samples ESP again, and finds the second sample four bytes higher, which is the callee having consumed it. A caller-cleaned model would leave the two samples equal.

slots.entry+4: the one ordinary argument: the key word, the only value the body ever compares

layout_derivation.note: 0x798 and 0x79c are the complete set the machine-derived receiver record enumerates (receiver.offsets [1944, 1948], register ECX, bounds_only true) and an independent alias-aware scan of the complete listing, which follows MOV ESI,ECX, reaches the same pair and nothing else. layout_derivation.stride 0xac: three instructions agree: 0x00fa55bd ADD EDX,0xac steps the scan cursor, 0x00fa55d5 IMUL ECX,ECX,0xac scales the matched index, and 0x00fa55f2 ADD dword ptr [ESI+0x79c],0xffffff54 subtracts it from the end word
layout_derivation.element key at +0xa8: 0x00fa55b2 LEA EDX,[EDI+0xa8] forms the address and 0x00fa55b8 CMP dword ptr [EDX],EBX is the only comparison the body makes against a 32-bit word other than the two addresses; 0xa8 + 4 == 0xac exactly, so the key ends the element
layout_derivation.context_from_other_listings: two sibling bodies in the same class read the same pair the same way and are corroboration only, not evidence from this body: 0x00fa72e3 forms the same count, then loads [esi] and [esi+4] as begin and end, compares (end-begin+0xac) against end, calls 0x00f9f770 with the same three-word shape and adds 0xffffff54 to [esi+4]; 0x00fa9d78 loads the same pair, calls 0x00f9f770 with (end, end, begin) and then adds ((end-begin)/0xac)*0xac to the second word. Neither is used to name anything here.

mechanics.control_flow: four conditional branches, all with absolute targets inside the recovered span 0x00fa5580..0x00fa5601: JLE 0x00fa55c7 (0x00fa55a6, the count <= 0 guard), JZ 0x00fa55cf (0x00fa55ba, the match), JL 0x00fa55b8 (0x00fa55c5, the loop bound) and JNC 0x00fa55f2 (0x00fa55e5, the unsigned shift guard). No unconditional jump, no indirect transfer, and no branch leaves the body.
mechanics.branch_polarity: the count guard is a SIGNED `<= 0` (TEST EAX,EAX / JLE), the loop bound is a SIGNED `<` against the same count and is tested AFTER the increment, and the shift guard is an UNSIGNED `>=` on two addresses (CMP EAX,EDX / JNC). The model reproduces each polarity rather than its C equivalent: `count > 0`, `index >= count` as the negation of a signed `<`, and an explicit std::uint32_t comparison for the address test.

count_arithmetic.instructions: 0x00fa5590 MOV EAX,0x2fa0be83 / 0x00fa5595 IMUL EDX / 0x00fa5597 SAR EDX,0x5 / 0x00fa559a MOV EAX,EDX / 0x00fa559c SHR EAX,0x1f / 0x00fa559f ADD EAX,EDX
count_arithmetic.identity: 0x2fa0be83 is 799063683 and 0x2fa0be83 * 0xac == 2^37 + 4 exactly, so the six instructions are the compiler's signed-division expansion for a divisor of 0xac, correction included
count_arithmetic.non_negative_span: equals span / 0xac exactly. Verified over every span in [0, 0x7fffffff] and at 0xac*k for k in [0, 12000]: zero divergences. The accumulated error is 4/2^37 per element, at most 0.063 of an element at the largest 32-bit span.
count_arithmetic.negative_span: does NOT equal the C result. SHR EAX,0x1f is a LOGICAL shift, so a negative quotient puts 0xffffffff in EAX and ADD EAX,EDX moves it one further from zero: the sequence returns floor(0x2fa0be83*span/2^37) - 1, which for a negative span is the truncating quotient minus one. Span -0xac gives -3 where C gives -1; span -0xac*256 gives -258 where C gives -256. This is a property of these six instructions and not an inference.
count_arithmetic.why_it_matters: a negative span cannot arise from a well-formed pair of pointers, but the two words are independent loads, so the model keeps the machine's arithmetic and the model test drives a negative span to separate the two. For a negative span both forms take the not-found arm (both counts are <= 0), so the difference is observable ONLY in the three dead bytes of the return register -- which is why the model publishes them as instrumentation.

return_word.not_found: EAX holds the count, then XOR AL,AL at 0x00fa55c9 clears only the low byte, so bits 8..31 are count & 0xffffff00 -- which is ZERO for any count below 256, including every well-formed non-empty array with fewer than 256 elements
return_word.found_no_shift: EAX holds the successor's address from 0x00fa55dd (LEA EAX,[ECX+0xac]), then MOV AL,0x1 at 0x00fa55fe
return_word.found_with_shift: EAX holds 0x00f9f770's own return word, because nothing writes EAX between the call at 0x00fa55ea and 0x00fa55fe. 0x00f9f770 returns its write cursor, which for this call is the new end (end - 0xac).
return_word.modelling: the C-visible return is the low byte, which is the whole of what the declared 1-byte type promises, and dead_return_word() publishes the full composed word. That publication is INSTRUMENTATION, declared as such in the header: a C++ model cannot pin the dead bytes of a return register, and the mandated -m32 g++ is free to zero them. The trampoline therefore asserts only that the low byte is the flag, and the model test asserts the published word against the machine's own composition rules, including a poisoned callee return so that the callee's contribution is separable from the successor's address.

mechanics.globals: none: the complete 46-instruction listing names no data-segment address, and the source span names none either (the class table's address is in the .cpp's file header comment, which is outside the target span).

direct_call_1.convention: cdecl: the callee's last three bytes are `5E C3` (POP ESI; RET) with no immediate, and the body drops the three words itself at 0x00fa55ef with `ADD ESP,0xc`
direct_call_1.arguments: three words pushed right to left at 0x00fa55e7..0x00fa55e9, so the callee sees (successor, limit, matched): EAX from 0x00fa55dd first, then EDX from 0x00fa55cf, then ECX from 0x00fa55db. The order is fixed by the callee's own three frame reads, not by its decompilation: 0x00f9f771 `MOV EBX,[ESP+0xc]` at ESP=entry-4 takes entry+8, i.e. the SECOND word; 0x00f9f776 `MOV ESI,[ESP+0xc]` at ESP=entry-8 takes entry+4, i.e. the FIRST; 0x00f9f77f `MOV EDI,[ESP+0x18]` at ESP=entry-12 takes entry+0xc, i.e. the THIRD.
direct_call_1.copy_direction: fixed by 0x00f9f620, not by the argument names, and this is the one place a two-level misreading would be silent. 0x00f9f622 `MOV EDI,[ESP+0xc]` takes its stack word, 0x00f9f627 `MOV ESI,ECX` takes its receiver, and 0x00f9f62e/0x00f9f631 do `FLD DWORD PTR [EDI+0x38]` / `FSTP DWORD PTR [ESI+0x38]` -- loading from the stack word and storing into the receiver. So in 0x00f9f770's loop the FIRST word is what is copied FROM and the THIRD is what is copied INTO, while the loop's exit test compares the first against the second. Read the other way round, the body would duplicate the element it removes instead of closing the gap.
direct_call_1.effect: for as long as the read cursor has not reached the limit, the element under it is copied into the element under the write cursor, both advancing by one 0xac stride, and the callee returns the write cursor. With this call site that is every element after the match moving down one slot. Number of moves = (limit - successor) / 0xac; the callee's own early exit (0x00f9f77a/0x00f9f77c) makes the call a no-op when the read cursor starts at the limit, which the caller's unsigned guard already prevents.
direct_call_1.return: the write cursor, dead for the array and NOT dead for the return word (see mechanics.return_word.found_with_shift)
direct_call_1.callee_record: no metadata record for this address; its shape and its copy direction were read from its own 0x38 bytes in the image

mechanics.receiver_writes: one: ADD dword ptr [ESI+0x79c],0xffffff54 at 0x00fa55f2, on BOTH arms -- including the arm where the shift was skipped, where it is the only mutation the body makes. The model test asserts at byte level that no byte of the receiver outside those four changes, by filling the whole receiver with a pattern first so an untouched byte is distinguishable from a zero the model happened to leave.
mechanics.not_modelled: the epilogue's register restores (EBX/ESI/EDI pops), which produce nothing observable; and the pair of extra loads of the receiver's two words (0x00fa5584/0x00fa55cf and 0x00fa558a/0x00fa55a8). The model reads each once, which is a statement that the second reads are not separable from inside the body -- nothing this body calls writes the receiver -- and not a claim that the machine loads each once. See unresolved_questions.

return_semantics.value: 0 when no element's +0xa8 word equals the argument, 1 when one did and the element was removed. No other value is producible: the two exits are XOR AL,AL and MOV AL,0x1.
return_semantics.width: one byte, fixed by the listing: no path writes the other three bytes of EAX before either return, and the C type among the 1-byte candidates (bool, char, uint8_t) is not recoverable from any record. uint8_t is declared because it asserts the width and nothing else.
return_semantics.ownership: The body performs no reference acquisition or release of its own. It reads two pointers out of the receiver and hands addresses to one callee; whether the array is owned, borrowed or a smart handle is not established by any record for this target and is not claimed.
return_semantics.lifetime: no object is created or destroyed here. The element that is removed keeps its own bytes in place -- the shift moves the elements AFTER it, and the end word then excludes the last slot -- so nothing in this body invalidates a pointer it handed out.

Two places where it loses information, both resolved in favour of the listing: (1) it writes the count as `(end - begin) / 0xac`, which is right for every non-negative span and wrong by one for every negative one, because the six instructions it stands for add a further -1 on a negative quotient; (2) it models the hidden receiver as `param_1` and so shows two parameters where the frame carries one argument word plus the ECX receiver. unresolved_questions: The only return claim any record carries for this VA is the machine-vocabulary phrase return_semantics 'integral_in_EAX', with return_register EAX and NO return_type field anywhere. That is not a C type, so the validator's string comparison against this package's declared std::uint8_t cannot pass, and RETURN SEMANTICS is a WARN for that reason alone. Declaring a typedef literally named integral_in_EAX would make the string match; that was NOT done, because inventing a C identifier to satisfy a comparison is the opposite of evidence-only, and the width the listing actually fixes (one byte) is asserted by the model and by the model test either way. This is the integrator's call if the aggregate matters more than the spelling.

What the array IS. Two words at +0x798 and +0x79c, a 0xac stride, a decrement on removal and an increment in a sibling all say 'a fixed-capacity array with a cursor'. No record names it, the 0x7a0 capacity word a sibling reads is not touched by this body, and nothing here says the key at an element's +0xa8 is a name, an id or a hash. No member is named for either receiver word and no element member is named except by its offset.

Why the key sits at +0xa8 of a 0xac record -- i.e. what the preceding 0xa8 bytes are. 0x00f9f620 copies dwords and then x87 floats across the record, so it is plainly a value-like record with a trailing word, but no record for it exists in this repository and none is claimed.

Whether the two extra loads of the receiver's two words (0x00fa5584 then 0x00fa55cf, and 0x00fa558a then 0x00fa55a8) are meaningful. Nothing this body calls writes the receiver, so no interleaving can be observed between the first load and the second, and the model reads each once. A mutation that cached the first load in place of the second SURVIVES the model test, which is the honest statement of that limit rather than a claim that the loads are equivalent.

Whether the class table's other 25 entries above this one at 0x01490be8 name the class. This binary has no MSVC RTTI, the xref export records vtable_reference_count 0 for this target, and the table association is a transitive classifier artifact (the validator's own source calls record['vtables'] a classifier association that contradicts the xref export). Nothing is named from it here, and the subsystem label 'Sporepedia' on this target comes from the queue record rather than from the model.

Whether the original C++ return type was bool, char or something else of one byte. The machine fixes the width and the two values; it does not fix the spelling, and no record supplies a return_type. uint8_t is declared as the spelling that asserts only the width.

validation.model_test: plain int main() with explicit checks, no framework and no external dependency. The one direct callee is defined in the test as an observer implementing 0x00f9f770's real semantics, recording its three arguments by identity, the number of moves, the receiver's +0x79c as it stands at the moment of the call, and the two neighbouring decoy words; it can also be made to return a poisoned word. The count helper is cross-checked against a second, independently written transliteration of the same six instructions. An inline-asm trampoline sets ECX, pushes the argument, samples ESP on both sides of the call and captures EAX, so the cleanup convention is measured rather than asserted. Cases: a match in the middle of three (arguments, order, copy direction, move count, decrement, decoys, dead bits); a match in the last element (the call is skipped and the decrement still happens); the loop bound from both sides; an empty array and a sub-stride span, both with the key present; the key offset driven in both directions with decoys at the element's +0x00 and at the receiver's neighbouring words; write ordering (the callee sees the pre-decrement limit and the full move count); the receiver's pair against a decoy array planted in the same object; the count table, the non-negative-span equivalence and the negative-span divergence; the dead return bits with a poisoned callee return; the measured ABI; a byte-level comparison of the whole receiver against a pre-filled pattern; and a three-element match at index count-1.
